scenes.headline: What computes the geometry in Steve
scenes.sub: A kernel, a solver, and an optional Blender
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Plumb! Let's see which engine in Steve draws the solids, and where Blender fits.

scenes.text: A Steve part is Python run against a feature API on the OpenCascade kernel, and Blender is a separate process that only receives meshes.
scenes.say: The idea: the solids come from OpenCascade. Blender is a separate process, and only receives meshes.

steps.say: A document is Python. It calls a feature API with named sketches, extrudes and holes.
Solids are built by OpenCascade, a kernel that keeps exact surfaces.
Sketch constraints go to planegcs, FreeCAD's solver, compiled to WebAssembly.
A Blender scene can link a part, but receives it as a glTF mesh, never as code.

scenes.title: Two ways to know a volume

left.title: OpenCascade part
left.say: In a part, a sphere is an equation, and its volume is exact.

right.title: Blender scene
right.say: In a Blender scene, volume is summed over triangles, and an open mesh has none.

scenes.title: Mesh volume error on a 10 mm sphere
scenes.say: Measured on a ten millimetre sphere, the mesh volume error falls about fourfold each time the longitudes double.

scenes.text: Steve's solids come from OpenCascade. Blender is fetched, pinned by hash, and kept behind a process boundary.

scenes.say: To recap: OpenCascade builds the solids, planegcs solves the sketches, and Blender only gets meshes.
